item.description:
Hertz Fellowship Application Deadline: 10/30/2026

The 2027 Hertz Fellowship application is live, and the search for the next cohort of Hertz Fellows is on. We're looking for creative problem solvers eager to tackle real-world problems. For over 60 years, the Hertz Fellowship has identified and supported graduate students in the applied sciences, engineering and mathematics who have bold ideas and the drive to pursue them, free from funding constraints.

Hertz Fellows receive up to five years of financial support (including a stipend and full tuition equivalent valued over $250,000), access to special programming for the entirety of their PhD and early career, lifelong mentorship and a Hertz Community of more than 1,300 exceptional innovators worldwide.

Program Information: https://www.hertzfoundation.org/the-fellowship/apply-for-fellowship/
Application Deadline: October 30, 2026
General Eligibility:
- College seniors, first-year graduate students, or in a gap year preparing to apply to graduate school (enrolled as first- or second-year PhD students in fall 2027 when funding would begin)
- Pursuing, or planning to pursue, a full-time PhD in the applied physical and biological sciences, mathematics or engineering at a U.S. institution
- Intend to direct their studies toward understanding and solving major, near-term problems facing society
- Citizens or permanent residents of the United States

We do not award fellowships to applicants pursuing professional degrees other than a PhD, such as an MD, JD, MBA, DPH, or DVM. However, we will support the PhD portion of an MD/PhD program.

 

Application Feedback:
Candidates are encouraged to consult with a faculty mentor or research advisor in their field of study for assistance with preparing application materials. Prospective candidates and candidates interested in receiving feedback on application drafts are also encouraged to schedule Office of Fellowships advising and draft feedback appointments with Gaylena Merritt, Director of Fellowships.

item.title: WIIT Trust Scholarship. Application Deadline: 11/01/2026
item.description:
WIIT Trust Scholarship. Application Deadline: 11/01/2026

WIIT Trust Scholarship is a merit-based scholarship offered by the Women in International Trade Charitable Trust to support women pursuing studies related to international trade, economic development, global business, supply chains, and women's economic empowerment.

Program Information: https://www.wiit.org/wiit-scholarships

Application Deadline: November 1, 2026

General Eligibility:

  • College juniors, seniors, or graduate students. Applicants must identify as female and be currently enrolled full-time or part-time at an accredited U.S. college or university.

  • Academic Interests: Applicants should demonstrate an interest in international trade, including trade policy, global business, economic development, or women's economic empowerment.

  • Essay Requirement: Applicants must submit an original, 5–10-page essay on a relevant international trade topic, along with a completed information sheet and university transcript.

Scholarship Benefits:

  • $3,000 scholarship applied toward academic costs.

  • One full year of personal mentorship from a WIIT member.

  • One full year of WIIT membership.

  • An opportunity to participate in a WIIT program related to the winning essay topic and engage with international trade professionals.

Application Feedback:

Applicants should review the official WIIT Trust Scholarship website for complete requirements and submission instructions.

Princeton in Latin America Fellowship Application Deadline: 11/01/2026

PiLA is a nonprofit organization affiliated with Princeton University that connects graduating seniors and recent graduates with year long professional fellowships at nonprofit and community-based organizations across Latin America and the Caribbean. Our fellowships offer opportunities to gain valuable professional experience, contribute to locally led initiatives, and engage in meaningful cross-cultural exchange.

Program Information: https://princetoninlatinamerica.org/
Application Deadline: November 1, 2026
General Eligibility:
- Bachelor’s degree. Some positions may require additional work experience or credentials. We do accept candidates with master’s degrees, but not those with terminal or professional degrees (e.g., Ph.D, medical, law, etc.). 

- College seniors or recent college graduates. There is no age limit for applying to PiA.

- PiA does not restrict eligibility based on US citizenship or residency status, but all candidates must present a compelling rationale for how they will contribute to PiA’s mission of United States-Asia exchange. Please note that host countries’ visa restrictions may limit our ability to place citizens of certain nationalities.

 

Application Feedback:

item.description:
American-Scandinavian Foundation (ASF) Fellowships for Americans Application Deadline: 11/1/2026

The American-Scandinavian Foundation (ASF) is accepting applications for Fellowships for Americans in the Nordic Countries in the 2027-28 academic year. 
ASF offers both long-term (4-12 months) fellowships of up to $23,000 and short-term (1-3 months) fellowships of up to $5,000 to graduate students (preferably dissertation-related) and academic professionals interested in pursuing research or creative arts projects in the Nordic region (Denmark, Faroe Islands, Greenland, Iceland, Finland, Norway, Sweden, and Sápmi). 
 
Program Information: https://www.amscan.org/fellowships-grants/grants-and-awards-for-americans/
Application Deadline: November 1, 2026
 
General Eligibility:

- Applicants must be United States citizens or permanent residents.
- Team projects are eligible, but each member must apply as an individual, submitting a separate, fully-documented application.
- Applicants must have completed their undergraduate education by the start of their project in the Nordic region.
- ASF considers it desirable that all candidates have at least some ability in the language of the host country, unless your project does not require the use of a Nordic language. For projects that require a command of one or more Nordic (or other) languages, candidates should defer application until they have the necessary proficiency.

Application Feedback:
Candidates are encouraged to consult with a faculty mentor or advisor in their field of study for assistance with preparing application materials. Prospective candidates and candidates interested in receiving feedback on application drafts are also encouraged to schedule Office of Fellowships advising and draft feedback appointments with Gaylena Merritt, Director of Fellowships.

item.title: Goldwater Summer Research Internship Program Application Deadline: 11/2/2026
item.description:
Goldwater Summer Research Internship Program Application Deadline: 11/2/2026

Note: This information is about the Goldwater Summer Research Internship Program. To learn more about the Goldwater Scholarship, click here.

The Goldwater Summer Research Internship Program will help college freshmen and sophomores build the skills, knowledge, and confidence to make informed career choices and compete for future scholarships and graduate school opportunities. The program is especially intended for undergraduates with limited access to research experiences.

Mentorship and Research Community

Goldwater interns will join collaborative research teams that include senior researchers, postdoctoral scholars, graduate students, and, importantly, other undergraduates.

The Internship

The Goldwater Summer Research Internship is a 10-week research opportunity for college freshmen and sophomores. Interns will gain hands-on experience in Chemistry, CISE, Engineering, Life Sciences, or Physics and Astronomy at academic and national laboratories across the United States.

Each project is managed independently and may have different eligibility criteria, schedules, expectations, and costs. Students should review each project description carefully, including details about start and end dates, prior experience requirements, housing, meals, and other site-specific information.

Funding

Each intern will receive $10,500 to cover the internship and internship-related expenses. Students should review the meal and housing costs listed for each site and budget accordingly and should also budget for transportation to and from the internship location.

Eligibility

-Students who will have completed their freshman or sophomore year of college by the summer of 2027
- U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident Status

How to Apply

Student Intern Application: https://www.goldwaterinternship.gov/intern-application

Students should review the project descriptions carefully, then submit an application, identifying up to two projects for which they would like to be considered.

Timeline

  • Internship website opens: August 21, 2026

  • Application deadline: November 2, 2026

  • Review period: November 2, 2026 – January 8, 2027

  • Internships announced: January 15, 2027

Selection Process

  • The Foundation will collect submitted applications and share each application with the mentors for the projects the student selected.

  • Project mentors will review the applications associated with their projects.

  • Mentors will recommend the student whose background and interests best align with their project.

  • The Foundation will review the selection information submitted by mentors.

  • The Foundation will announce the Goldwater Summer Research Internship awards.

  • Intern Community and Scholarship Preparation

Interns will participate in a weekly Zoom meeting designed to build community across the Goldwater intern cohort. These meetings will include a workshop to help interns begin preparing Goldwater Scholarship applications. After completing the internship, interns are expected to apply for a Goldwater Scholarship through their home institutions in the fall.

From Monday, November 2, 2026 5:00 PM to 5:01 PM EST at Online.

item.description:
A Conversation About Vaccines (Q&A)

Vaccines are among the most discussed topics in medicine and one of the hardest to talk about openly. This event is a space to do exactly that.

Dr. Joel “Gator” Warsh is a board-certified pediatrician who practices integrative medicine in Los Angeles. He completed his pediatric training at Children’s Hospital Los Angeles, runs Integrative Pediatrics and Medicine in Studio City, and has published peer-reviewed research on childhood health. He is known for engaging directly with parents’ and patients’ toughest questions about vaccines, and he won’t sidestep the hard ones.

After a brief introduction, most of the evening will be an open Q&A. We’ll look at what the current research says about vaccines and vaccine safety: how vaccines are studied, how safety is monitored, where the evidence is strong, and where open questions remain. Whether you’re pre-med, a science major, a skeptic, a strong vaccine advocate, or just curious, bring your questions. The more challenging, the better.

item.description:
Deliberative (D) Teams - REGISTER BY SEPT. 3!
 
Davidson College’s Deliberative Citizenship Initiative (DCI) is dedicated to improving our civic discourse and invites you to participate in a Deliberative “D” Team. D Teams are small intergenerational groups of 6 to 12 people guided by DCI-trained facilitators who meet regularly to discuss important but difficult issues facing society.
 
CLICK HERE TO REGISTER for a Virtual or In-person meeting

This fall participants will engage in three 2-hour small-group discussions about topics that connect timeless themes – technological change, economic fairness, and the meaning of freedom – with highly-salient policy issues:
  • The Future of AI: What We Will Gain, What Will We Lose, and What Should We Do About It (Week of Sept. 28)
  • Affordability, Opportunity, and Social Well-Being: Economic Fairness and the Proper Role of Government (Week of Oct. 19)
  • What Does It Mean to Be Free? Guns, Drugs and Death (Week of Nov. 9)
Meeting with the same group of people for all three meetings helps participants get to know each other and build a sense of trust and community. D Teams provide a practical and accessible opportunity for individuals to engage across their social and political differences, practice their deliberative skills, and explore both areas of agreement and disagreement.

This year, we welcome participants from 24 colleges and universities that are the inaugural members of our new Deliberative Citizenship Network (DCN), a national initiative to assist higher education institutions in expanding their civil discourse programs. Participants not located in Davidson will join virtual D Teams that will enable them to connect with people from across the country. Participants located in Davidson will be able to join either virtual or in-person D Teams that will meet on the Davidson campus. 

Please complete the information below by Wed., Sept. 3 if you would like to join us for these important and rewarding conversations! Your responses are confidential and will help us create teams with a variety of perspectives on them. If you have any questions, please email dci@davidson.edu.

The Mississippi Teacher Corps (MTC) program at the University of Mississippi provides training and licensure for non-education majors who wish to teach grades 7-12.

Main benefits:

  • Full scholarship for a Master of Arts in Teaching from the University of Mississippi (covers all tuition, books, and fees)

  • Job placement in a Mississippi public school with full salary and benefits from the school district

  • Class A teaching license in Mississippi

  • Summer stipend to help cover moving and incidental expenses

  • Free on-campus housing during the summer training program

  • Mentoring and support from the MTC administration, second-year teachers, and alumni

 

Program Information: https://www.mtc.olemiss.edu/

Application Deadlines: 

· November 15: Early acceptance (decision sent by January 1)
· February 15: Preferred deadline
· April 15: Final deadline

General Eligibility:

- An undergraduate degree with coursework (12-18 hours, depending on the subject) related to at least one of the following areas: math, science, English, social studies, or a foreign language.
- A minimum 3.0 GPA in undergraduate coursework. If your GPA does not meet this requirement or your undergraduate school did not use a GPA system, you can meet the Praxis Core requirement by passing the Praxis Core test or having a 21 or higher composite score on the ACT.
- Passing score on the Praxis II test in the subject area you wish to teach.
- Participants must have a valid social security number and provide the Mississippi Department of Education with proof of lawful presence in the US.

 

If you would like to learn more about MTC, please email mtc@olemiss.edu and/or visit the Mississippi Teacher Corps website.

Have an idea for how to solve a problem you deal with every day? IdeaSprint gives you five weeks to actually try building a solution.

At the end of the five weeks, teams will present what they built at the Hurt Hub Innovation & Entrepreneurship Showcase on November 18. Attendees will vote for their favorite project, and the winning team will receive a $1,000 grand prize to keep developing their idea.
